impact_scope.description: The anchored VP8 quirk callable surface gains handling for the new QUIRK_HAS_ALPHA_SIDE_CHANNEL configuration key.

evidence: In S0, decoder.get_quirk and decoder.set_quirk! already form the public VP8 quirk callable surface.
H0 instantiates a wuffs_webp__decoder and never directly calls the VP8 decoder's get_quirk or set_quirk functions.
In S1, the same decoder.get_quirk and decoder.set_quirk! surface adds QUIRK_HAS_ALPHA_SIDE_CHANNEL handling.
H0 remains unchanged and still does not directly call or control the VP8 quirk API.
The WebP decoder sets the new VP8 quirk internally when it encounters an ALPH chunk, so H0 can reach the new behavior through its existing WebP input and decode path.

new_harness_obligation.description: No new H0 call, caller-supplied configuration, buffer arrangement, or call-order transition is required; the existing WebP path detects ALPH input, sets the VP8 quirk internally, and obtains the adjusted work-buffer length through the existing image-decoder interface.
evidence: H0 already passes arbitrary input to wuffs_webp__decoder through fuzz_image_decoder.
S1's decoder.do_decode_frame! calls vp8.set_quirk!(QUIRK_HAS_ALPHA_SIDE_CHANNEL, 1) internally after decoding an ALPH chunk.
H0 already queries workbuf_len and supplies that allocated buffer to decode_frame.

reason: The anchored public quirk functions existed in both states and their direct exposure was omitted by H0 in both states. The added key changes behavior within that same callable surface, while H0's existing one-hop WebP caller supplies the configuration automatically. Therefore the same-scope gap remains true before and after without a concrete new H0 action.
